citation: Liu, Stambaugh & Yuan (2019), Size and Value in China
economic_mechanism: China-specific value, size and shell-value mechanisms
a_share_evidence: Earnings-to-price is central to the CH-3 value factor; smallest firms require special interpretation because shell value can distort size and value
international_evidence: Value and size are classic global factors
expected_relationship: Higher earnings yield is favorable; size is not assumed to be a monotone alpha in the current sample
possible_redundancy: Book-to-price and size can overlap with shell-value exposure
complementary_role: Motivates earnings, book, sales and cash-flow valuation separation plus visible size diagnostics
turnover_implication: Value is usually slower moving; microcaps raise implementation concerns
design_impact: Value sleeve is subfamily-balanced; size is a diagnostic/control rather than a sleeve

citation: Jansen, Swinkels & Zhou (2021), Anomalies in the China A-share Market
a_share_evidence: Value, risk and trading carry over; size, quality and past-return evidence is weaker except residual momentum and reversal
international_evidence: Compares Chinese evidence with established international anomalies
expected_relationship: Positive value; low risk; low speculative trading; reversal; residual momentum
possible_redundancy: Risk measures and trading signals can be internally redundant
complementary_role: Sets prior strength and requires traditional momentum, reversal and risk mechanisms to remain distinct
design_impact: Strong priors for value/risk/trading/reversal; mixed priors for quality and raw momentum

citation: Leippold, Wang & Zhou (2022), Machine Learning in the Chinese Stock Market
economic_mechanism: Retail participation, liquidity and horizon-dependent predictability
a_share_evidence: Liquidity is the most important predictor in their broad ML study; transaction costs materially matter; size and ownership effects vary by horizon
expected_relationship: Liquidity/trading information can predict but must survive costs
possible_redundancy: Many technical features may rediscover the same liquidity state
complementary_role: Motivates separate liquidity level, speculative activity, price impact and flow diagnostics
turnover_implication: High relevance; raw predictability can be consumed by trading costs
design_impact: No ML is used here; liquidity is split into mechanisms and tested with P01 costs

citation: Hsu, Viswanathan, Wang & Wool (2018), Anomalies in Chinese A-Shares
economic_mechanism: Institutional structure, retail behavior and China-tailored factor design
a_share_evidence: Value and size can work under tailored construction; ordinary A-share momentum can reverse direction; overnight sentiment is relevant
international_evidence: Starts from US anomaly definitions and documents important China differences
expected_relationship: Do not flip raw momentum after observing results; high overnight sentiment is predeclared as overpricing
possible_redundancy: Momentum, reversal and overnight returns can look mechanically similar
complementary_role: Motivates competing raw-momentum and reversal sleeves and the negative overnight direction
turnover_implication: Short-horizon reversal and overnight signals imply turnover
design_impact: Traditional momentum remains a competing hypothesis and cannot be relabeled

citation: Pan, Tang & Xu (2014), Speculative Trading and Stock Returns
a_share_evidence: Abnormal turnover predicts lower future returns while past average turnover does not
expected_relationship: Higher abnormal turnover predicts lower returns
possible_redundancy: Abnormal turnover overlaps with volume ratio and amount shocks
complementary_role: Separates speculative activity from ordinary liquidity level
turnover_implication: High turnover is both the signal and an implementation warning
design_impact: Abnormal activity signals receive negative signs and subfamily balancing

citation: Wan (2018), Is the idiosyncratic volatility anomaly driven by the MAX or MIN effect?
economic_mechanism: Lottery preference and limits to arbitrage
a_share_evidence: Strong IVOL and MAX effects; IVOL is not subsumed by MAX in China
international_evidence: MAX often subsumes IVOL in US/European evidence
expected_relationship: Lower IVOL and lower MAX predict higher returns
possible_redundancy: IVOL, total volatility and MAX are correlated but economically non-identical
complementary_role: Supports retaining residual-risk and lottery-payoff subfamilies
turnover_implication: Low-risk signals are usually moderate turnover
design_impact: Low-risk sleeve balances IVOL and MAX rather than choosing one representative

citation: Residual momentum and the cross-section of stock returns: Chinese evidence (2019)
economic_mechanism: Continuation in factor-residual rather than raw returns
a_share_evidence: Residual momentum is significant and does not show long-run reversal
possible_redundancy: Residual and raw momentum should not be treated as equivalent
complementary_role: Defines a missing mechanism that the current matrix cannot honestly proxy
turnover_implication: Moderate turnover; requires a factor-model residual estimation step
design_impact: Residual momentum is documented in the map but excluded from V1 sleeves because no precomputed PIT residual factor exists

citation: George & Hwang (2004), The 52-Week High and Momentum Investing
economic_mechanism: Anchoring to a salient past price level
a_share_evidence: China-specific evidence is less mature than reversal/risk evidence
international_evidence: 52-week-high information can subsume part of raw momentum internationally
expected_relationship: Closer to the 52-week high predicts continuation
possible_redundancy: Correlated with raw momentum but measures an anchor rather than cumulative return
design_impact: 52-week high is separated from traditional momentum

economic_mechanism: Price response per unit of traded currency as illiquidity
a_share_evidence: Widely applied in A-share research but local turnover/speculation semantics differ
international_evidence: Positive illiquidity-return relation is a classic result
expected_relationship: Higher price impact may earn a gross premium
possible_redundancy: Amihud overlaps with volatility and small size
complementary_role: Adds price-impact information distinct from turnover
turnover_implication: Directly warns of trading capacity and costs
design_impact: Creates a one-factor price-impact sleeve with explicit cost warning

citation: Novy-Marx (2013), The Other Side of Value: The Gross Profitability Premium
economic_mechanism: Productive firms can earn higher returns even after controlling for value
a_share_evidence: A-share reviews find profitability/quality evidence less consistent
possible_redundancy: Profitability overlaps with value and margins
complementary_role: Tests whether fundamentals add to value
turnover_implication: Low turnover because accounting data updates slowly
design_impact: Profitability is complementary and its incremental value is explicitly tested

citation: Sloan (1996), Do Stock Prices Fully Reflect Information in Accruals and Cash Flows?
economic_mechanism: Earnings backed by cash are more persistent than accrual-heavy earnings
a_share_evidence: Chinese accounting evidence is mixed and reporting regimes evolved
international_evidence: Classic negative accrual and positive cash-flow-quality evidence
expected_relationship: Lower accruals and stronger cash backing are favorable
possible_redundancy: Accruals and operating cash flow are accounting identities with overlap
design_impact: Accruals are signed negative before outcomes and balanced against cash-generation measures

citation: Green, Hand & Zhang (2017), The Characteristics that Provide Independent Information about Average U.S. Monthly Stock Returns
economic_mechanism: Incremental information among a crowded characteristic set
a_share_evidence: Not China-specific and therefore used only as research-governance guidance
international_evidence: Many published characteristics are redundant once considered jointly
expected_relationship: No factor direction imported mechanically into China
complementary_role: Motivates explicit A vs A+B and residual-score diagnostics
turnover_implication: Redundant signals can increase turnover without information gain
design_impact: No one-representative cluster rule; subfamily balancing and limited incremental comparisons are used

economic_mechanism: Replication, microcap sensitivity and multiple-testing discipline
a_share_evidence: Not China-specific; recent Chinese replications also warn about microcap-weighted results
international_evidence: Many anomaly claims weaken under robust construction
expected_relationship: No result-driven sign or winner inference
possible_redundancy: Data mining and highly correlated variants inflate apparent evidence
complementary_role: Supports conservative priors and visible size exposure
turnover_implication: Microcaps and equal weighting can overstate implementability
design_impact: 765 data-qualified factors are not treated as 765 independent economic bets
